title: Keycloak
subtitle: Open-source identity and access management with SSO, OIDC and SAML.

tiles.label: OpenID Connect
tiles.says: Keycloak issues OIDC tokens through the authorization code flow.
tiles.detail: Applications delegate login and receive ID and access tokens. PKCE protects public clients and one login covers many apps.

tiles.label: SAML 2.0
tiles.says: Keycloak speaks SAML to enterprise applications.
tiles.detail: Legacy and SaaS apps federate with the same realm, which removes duplicate user databases.

tiles.label: JWT & JWKS
tiles.says: Signed tokens are verified offline with published keys.
tiles.detail: Gateways validate signature, issuer, audience and expiry without calling Keycloak per request, which keeps APIs fast.

tiles.label: Realms
tiles.says: Realms isolate users, clients and settings.
tiles.detail: Each realm is a security boundary, so environments or tenants never share identities.

tiles.label: Federation
tiles.says: User federation links LDAP, Active Directory and social logins.
tiles.detail: Existing directories remain the source of truth, so onboarding and offboarding stay consistent.

tiles.label: Auth flows
tiles.says: Flows add MFA, OTP and WebAuthn steps.
tiles.detail: Authentication sequences are configurable per client. Stronger assurance applies where risk is higher.

tiles.label: Roles & groups
tiles.says: Roles and groups map people to permissions.
tiles.detail: Claims in tokens carry roles that APIs enforce, centralising access decisions.

tiles.label: Clients & scopes
tiles.says: Clients define who may request which scopes.
tiles.detail: Redirect URIs, secrets and scopes limit what each application can obtain.

tiles.label: Sessions & events
tiles.says: Sessions can be revoked, and events are logged.
tiles.detail: Admin and login events support audits, and refresh tokens expire on policy.

declarations: Tokens are signed, short-lived and verifiable offline.
